prompt: Sort the order lines into margin bands. A line's margin is net_revenue_eur minus units times unit_cost_eur. margin_band is the text 'unknown' when net_revenue_eur, units or unit_cost_eur is missing; 'loss' when the margin is below 0; 'thin' when the margin is 0 or more but below 20 percent of net_revenue_eur; and 'healthy' for every other line. Use the sales table. Return three columns, in this order: channel, margin_band and n_lines, the number of order lines. Return one row per channel and margin_band combination that has at least one line. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per channel and margin band

hints: Next, write the column margin_band with its four branches, count the lines, and decide what one row stands for.

A margin worked out from a missing value is missing, and a missing value fails every < test, so ELSE would call it healthy: test for missing values first. A loss is also below 20 percent, so the loss test goes above the thin test.
why_this_works: The missing-value test runs first so no incomplete line is called healthy, and the loss test sits above the thin test because every loss is also below 20 percent.
